summary: WebSocket auth fixes have a critical X-Forwarded-For spoofing bypass; agent.py SSE fix has a NameError crash path when the first yield fails; dual auth between middleware and verify_api_key is inconsistent; health endpoints remain locked behind API key auth breaking K8s probes.

bugs.title: X-Forwarded-For spoofing allows remote auth bypass on WebSocket endpoints
bugs.detail: Both audio.py (line 24-27) and websocket.py (line 17-20) blindly trust the X-Forwarded-For header to determine client IP for the localhost auth bypass. A remote attacker can send `X-Forwarded-For: 127.0.0.1` and bypass API key authentication entirely. This affects both WebSocket auth checks AND the verify_api_key dependency in middleware_security.py (line 155-160). The fix is to only trust X-Forwarded-For when the direct peer is a known proxy, or to skip X-Forwarded-For for auth decisions entirely.

bugs.title: agent.py exception handler crashes with NameError when first yield fails
bugs.detail: In agent.py event_stream(), `full_response` is initialized at line 66 AFTER the first yield at line 64. If the first yield (meta event) raises an exception, `full_response` is never assigned. The except block at line 76 then evaluates `if full_response:` which raises NameError. This means the exception handler itself crashes, no terminal event is ever yielded, and the client hangs indefinitely. GeneratorExit (from client disconnect) inherits from BaseException, not Exception, so it propagates correctly. But any other RuntimeError in the first yield would trigger this crash. Fix: move `full_response = []` before the try block.

bugs.title: main.py middleware uses non-constant-time string comparison for API key
bugs.detail: The api_key_middleware in main.py (line 214) uses `api_key != BACKEND_API_KEY` which is not constant-time. The verify_api_key dependency (middleware_security.py:179) correctly uses `hmac.compare_digest`. The middleware applies to ALL /api/ routes including agent routes, creating dual auth where the weaker check runs first. This is a timing side-channel vulnerability for the REST API auth gate.

bugs.title: main.py middleware lacks X-Forwarded-For support for proxy-aware IP detection
bugs.detail: The middleware (main.py:211) uses `request.client.host` directly instead of using the `get_client_ip()` helper. When behind a reverse proxy (nginx, Traefik), `request.client.host` is always the proxy's IP (e.g., 127.0.0.1), so the localhost bypass always passes, and ALL proxied requests bypass auth. Conversely, if the proxy is on a different machine, localhost bypass never works for legitimate local requests. Fix: use `get_client_ip(request)` consistently.

bugs.title: Health endpoints locked behind API key auth — breaks K8s/Docker probes
bugs.detail: Both `/api/v1/health` (health.py) and `/api/v1/agent/health` (agent.py) are under the `/api/` prefix, so the middleware gates them. When BACKEND_API_KEY is set, Kubernetes liveness/readiness probes and Docker health checks cannot provide custom X-API-Key headers, causing probes to fail with 403. The root `/` endpoint is unauthenticated and could serve as a health check, but health.py provides richer data (uptime, memory, cpu) that probes need. Fix: exclude /health paths from middleware auth, or use the root endpoint for probes.

bugs.title: audio.py WebSocket auth silently drops unauthorized connections with no log
bugs.detail: When an invalid API key is provided on the audio WebSocket, audio.py (line 38) closes with code 1008 but does not log the event. websocket.py (line 43) correctly logs a warning. This creates a security visibility gap — unauthorized WebSocket connection attempts to `/audio/ws` go undetected in logs. Fix: add `logger.warning(...)` before `await websocket.close(code=1008)`.

bugs.title: resolvePlaybackRef leaked when requestTTSStream() interleaves with speak()
bugs.detail: The `requestTTSStream()` method (useAudioWS.ts:142) calls `stopCurrentAudio()` but does not resolve `resolvePlaybackRef`. If `speak()` was called first and established a promise, then `requestTTSStream()` is called, the old speak promise hangs unresolved. The `speak()` method correctly chains the old resolve before setting a new one, but `requestTTSStream()` does not. Fix: call `resolvePlaybackRef.current?.()` at the start of `requestTTSStream()`.

bugs.title: Race: stale audio onended/onerror closures retain references after guard short-circuit
bugs.detail: When `playAudioBlob()` is called rapidly, old audio elements' `onended`/`onerror` callbacks are guarded by `if (activeAudioRef.current !== audio) return;` and return early. However, the closure still holds references to `audio`, `url`, `cleanup`, `objectUrlsRef`, `activeAudioRef`, etc. This creates a minor memory leak where old HTMLAudioElement instances and their closure chains survive until GC runs. Under rapid TTS streaming, this could accumulate. Fix: nullify `onended`/`onerror` on the old audio element in `stopCurrentAudio()`.

bugs.title: TTS zero-chunk from both providers yields silent empty stream
bugs.detail: The `synthesize_stream` fix correctly handles OpenAI yielding zero chunks by falling through to Edge TTS. However, if Edge TTS ALSO yields zero chunks (e.g., empty input after validation, or edge-tts not installed), the async generator completes with no chunks yielded and no error raised. The caller in audio.py sends `tts_end` with zero chunks, and the client silently does nothing. Edge TTS yielding zero chunks is rare but possible if the text is empty after language processing. Fix: add a `yielded` check after Edge TTS stream and yield a sentinel or raise if still false.

bugs.title: WebSocket onmessage catch block silently swallows all parse errors
bugs.detail: useAudioWS.ts line 112-114 has an empty catch block `catch { // skip }`. Any JSON parse errors or message handling exceptions are silently swallowed. While this prevents crashes from malformed messages, it also hides real bugs. Fix: log the error (at least in development) and set error state.

bugs.title: _get_client_ip duplicated in three files with identical logic
bugs.detail: The `_get_client_ip(websocket)` function is duplicated verbatim in audio.py and websocket.py, and `get_client_ip(request)` exists in middleware_security.py with the same logic (different parameter type). Any fix to one (e.g., adding trusted proxy IPs) must be replicated to all three. This is a maintenance burden and a source of future inconsistencies. Fix: extract into a shared utility, e.g., `utils/client_ip.py`.

bugs.title: Redundant dual auth on agent routes — middleware + Depends both check API key
bugs.detail: Agent router routes pass through BOTH the api_key_middleware (main.py:204-219, covers all /api/ routes) AND the router-level Depends(verify_api_key) (agent.py:17). The middleware uses weak comparison (string !=) and no X-Forwarded-For support, while the dependency uses constant-time comparison and proxy-aware IP detection. The middleware check is strictly weaker but runs first. This is redundant, inconsistent, and confusing. Fix: remove the middleware auth for /api/v1/agent/* and rely solely on the router-level dependency (or vice versa, standardized).

impact.affectedSystems: All authenticated WebSocket endpoints (audio, chat), agent SSE streaming, REST API auth gate, Kubernetes/Docker health probes, audio playback hook
impact.userImpact: P0: Remote attacker can bypass auth on all WebSocket endpoints by spoofing X-Forwarded-For header. P0: SSE agent stream can silently hang clients if first yield fails. P1: K8s deployments will fail health checks. P1: Timing attack surface on REST API key check. P1: Behind-proxy deployments have broken auth.

rootCause: Three systemic issues: (1) Trusting X-Forwarded-For without verifying the immediate peer (WebSocket auth bypass). (2) Variable-initialization ordering bug in agent.py exception handler that crashes the catcher. (3) Two parallel auth systems (middleware + dependency) that use different comparison methods and IP-detection logic, creating inconsistency and a veiled timing side-channel. The remaining items stem from incomplete coverage (no logging, leaked promises, unextracted utility).

fixPlan.title: Fix X-Forwarded-For spoofing on WebSocket auth and verify_api_key
fixPlan.action: In _get_client_ip (audio.py, websocket.py) and get_client_ip (middleware_security.py), do NOT trust X-Forwarded-For for localhost detection. Either (a) remove X-Forwarded-For entirely from the auth path and use only the direct socket IP, or (b) add a TRUSTED_PROXIES config and only respect X-Forwarded-For when the immediate peer IP is in that list. Option (a) is simpler and safer for now. Rewrite: `return websocket.client.host if websocket.client else ""` (no X-Forwarded-For).
fixPlan.codeHint: In audio.py:23-27, websocket.py:17-21, middleware_security.py:155-160 — Remove the X-Forwarded-For block entirely. Return `websocket.client.host` / `request.client.host` directly.

fixPlan.title: Fix agent.py full_response NameError in exception handler
fixPlan.action: Move `full_response = []` initialization outside the try block (before `try:`) so it's guaranteed to be defined even if the first yield raises. This ensures the exception handler can always access it without a NameError.
fixPlan.codeHint: In agent.py, change: move `full_response = []` from line 66 to before `try:` on line 63. The try block should start after initialization.

fixPlan.title: Fix main.py middleware to use constant-time comparison and proxy-aware IP
fixPlan.action: Replace the string `!=` comparison with `hmac.compare_digest`. Use `get_client_ip(request)` from middleware_security.py instead of `request.client.host` directly for consistency with the rest of the auth system. These two changes align the middleware with verify_api_key and eliminate the timing side-channel.
fixPlan.codeHint: In main.py:214, change `if api_key != BACKEND_API_KEY and not is_local:` to use `hmac.compare_digest`. Add `from utils.middleware_security import get_client_ip` and use it on line 211 instead of `request.client.host`.

fixPlan.title: Exclude health endpoints from API key auth
fixPlan.action: Add exceptions in main.py middleware for `/api/v1/health` and `/api/v1/agent/health` paths. The simplest approach: add a prefix skip list at the top of the middleware. Also remove `Depends(verify_api_key)` from the agent router's /health route specifically (or add an exclude). K8s probes can then hit either endpoint without auth.
fixPlan.codeHint: In main.py:207, add before the auth check: `if request.url.path in (\"/api/v1/health\", \"/api/v1/agent/health\"): return await call_next(request)`. And in agent.py:91, consider excluding /health from the router dependency (add `dependencies=[]` override on that route).

fixPlan.title: Add auth-failure logging to audio.py WebSocket
fixPlan.action: Add `logger.warning(...)` before `await websocket.close(code=1008)` in audio.py to match the logging in websocket.py.
fixPlan.codeHint: In audio.py:37, add `logger.warning(\"Unauthorized Audio WS connection attempt (bad API key)\")` before the close.

fixPlan.title: Fix resolvePlaybackRef leak in requestTTSStream
fixPlan.action: Call `resolvePlaybackRef.current?.()` at the start of `requestTTSStream()` before calling `stopCurrentAudio()`. This ensures any pending speak() promise is properly resolved when requestTTSStream interrupts playback.
fixPlan.codeHint: In useAudioWS.ts:142-148, add `resolvePlaybackRef.current?.(); resolvePlaybackRef.current = null;` at the top of requestTTSStream before stopCurrentAudio().

fixPlan.title: Nullify old audio element event handlers in stopCurrentAudio
fixPlan.action: In stopCurrentAudio(), after pausing the audio, set `activeAudioRef.current.onended = null` and `activeAudioRef.current.onerror = null` to release closure references and prevent stale callbacks from retaining memory.
fixPlan.codeHint: In useAudioWS.ts:27-30, after `activeAudioRef.current.pause()`, add `activeAudioRef.current.onended = null; activeAudioRef.current.onerror = null;`

fixPlan.title: Extract _get_client_ip into shared utility module
fixPlan.action: Create `backend/utils/client_ip.py` with a single function `get_client_ip(host_provider: HasClientHost | HasHeaders)` that works for both Request and WebSocket via duck-typing or overloads. Import and use it from audio.py, websocket.py, and middleware_security.py.
fixPlan.codeHint: Create `utils/client_ip.py`: `def get_client_ip(request_or_ws): forwarded = request_or_ws.headers.get(\"x-forwarded-for\", \""); if forwarded: return forwarded.split(\",\")[0].strip(); client = getattr(request_or_ws, \"client\", None); return client.host if client else \"\"`

fixPlan.title: Add yielding guard for TSS zero-chunk edge case
fixPlan.action: After the Edge TTS stream loop in `synthesize_stream`, check if `yielded` is still False (meaning neither provider yielded anything). If so, yield a sentinel empty bytes object or log a warning. The audio.py caller already handles `tts_end` with zero chunks, but the silent failure should be visible in logs.
fixPlan.codeHint: In tts.py:40-41, after Edge TTS for loop, add `if not yielded: logger.warning(\"TTS stream yielded zero chunks from both providers\")`

fixPlan.title: Consolidate dual auth on agent routes
fixPlan.action: Once the middleware is fixed (step 3), evaluate whether the middleware-level check for agent routes is still needed. Since agent routes already have Depends(verify_api_key), the middleware gate is redundant. Either: (a) remove the middleware auth entirely and rely on per-router dependencies, or (b) remove the router dependency and keep middleware (simpler, one auth point). Option (a) is cleaner. Then remove `Depends(verify_api_key)` from agent.py:17 and move it to each route individually where needed, excluding /health.
fixPlan.codeHint: In agent.py:17, remove `dependencies=[Depends(verify_api_key)]` from the router. Add `Depends(verify_api_key)` to /chat, /stream, and /rag endpoints individually. Exclude /health.

prevention: 1. Security: Never trust client-supplied headers (X-Forwarded-For) for auth decisions without verifying the immediate peer. Use a TrustedProxies config or skip the header entirely in auth paths. 2. Code patterns: Always initialize variables before try blocks they're used in within except handlers. 3. Auth architecture: Pick ONE auth mechanism (middleware OR route dependency), not both. Standardize on hmac.compare_digest everywhere. 4. Async closures: Always nullify event handlers on DOM elements before discarding them to prevent closure memory leaks. 5. Promise lifecycle: Every code path that interrupts an async operation must resolve or reject the associated promise. 6. Logging: All auth failures must be logged for security auditing. 7. Health endpoints: Must always be exempt from auth for operational tooling.
testCases: TEST 1 (X-Forwarded-For spoofing): Connect to /ws/audio with X-Forwarded-For: 127.0.0.1 and no api_key. ASSERT: connection is rejected with code 1008 (NOT accepted).
TEST 2 (X-Forwarded-For spoofing): POST to /api/v1/agent/chat with X-Forwarded-For: 127.0.0.1 and no X-API-Key. ASSERT: returns 403 (NOT 200).
TEST 3 (agent SSE first-yield failure): Mock a scenario where streaming response meta event fails (e.g., mock the generator). ASSERT: client receives an 'error' event (not hangs indefinitely).
TEST 4 (health endpoint auth exclusion): GET /api/v1/health with BACKEND_API_KEY set. ASSERT: returns 200 without X-API-Key header.

TEST 5 (main.py middleware constant-time): POST to /api/v1/system/status with wrong X-API-Key. ASSERT: returns 403. Test timing variance is statistically insignificant (automated timing attack probe).
TEST 6 (audio.py auth logging): Connect to /audio/ws with wrong api_key. ASSERT: log file contains warning about unauthorized connection.
TEST 7 (resolvePlaybackRef leak): Call speak() then immediately requestTTSStream(). ASSERT: speak() promise resolves (doesn't hang).
TEST 8 (TTS zero-chunk): Call synthesize_stream with empty/malformed text where both providers yield nothing. ASSERT: warning is logged; audio.py sends tts_end with empty chunks.
TEST 9 (main.py localhost behind proxy): Set X-Forwarded-For to 127.0.0.1 and connect from non-local IP. ASSERT: middleware does NOT bypass auth (because direct socket IP is not local).
TEST 10 (memory leak): Call playAudioBlob 100 times rapidly. ASSERT: no more than 5 active HTMLAudioElement instances exist after each cycle; memory usage is stable.
